author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Heavy rain flooded the Oaklawn Avenue underpass in Cranston on Sunday, trapping vehicles below the bike-path bridge and renewing calls for a permanent solution, NBC 10 reported.

The low-lying road between Oaklawn Avenue and Wilbur Avenue can fill with a foot or more of water during intense rain. A nearby worker told the station he has seen the underpass flood about 50 times over six years.

Residents said cars can become stranded quickly when the roadway is not closed before drivers reach the water. Solar-powered warning lights have been installed, but some people told NBC 10 they rarely see them operating, especially during the day.

The flooding has become a recurring safety and transportation problem rather than a one-time storm impact. Drivers who enter the water risk damaging their vehicles and blocking access for emergency crews.

The Rhode Island Department of Transportation, which maintains the bike-path bridge, said it has been in contact with Cranston and is pursuing a Federal Emergency Management Agency grant. The city had not responded to the station’s request for comment.
dek: Water filled the Oaklawn Avenue underpass during heavy rain Sunday, trapping vehicles below the bike-path bridge.
headline: Cranston underpass floods again as residents press for long-term fix
